Wow, you made a pretty big mistake to end up here. I hope you're not trying to steal a dungeon or something...
I'll send you back to the warehouse just in case.
The hunt has begun and the prey is in our lair! To arms, my friends! To teeth and claws and paws! What fun!
Hold! Let us parlay, that I might speak my piece before you wrest the very life from my body. Let us duel with words, to see if some mutual benefit might be found.

His friend was Halaster, then a young but still powerful mage. I confided my fears to Halaster when he told me about the lycanthropy. He offered me a potion that he used to keep himself young, warning that it was terribly addictive.

I took the potion and became addicted, but Halaster went mad and I ended up following him here, in hopes of getting the recipe for the potion. He trapped me here and forced me to fight for him, in return for the potion.

This is not a natural setting for a man of my tastes and I long to leave here and never return. My spirit cries out for the feel of the grass, the sounds of the forest, the scent of the prey and the taste of wine.

The Baccha family was notorious for our parties. These were revelries where drinking was the path, and pleasure the only goal. Friends would come for miles around and stay for weeks, even months. All of noble birth, plus those who amused us, were invited.
I suppose there were a few of those. Well, truthfully, we weren't terribly selective: whores, poets, bards, clowns, clumsy peasants and other oddities to upper-class society.
It could be. Truthfully, we weren't terribly selective about who could come to our parties: whores, poets, bards, clowns, clumsy peasants and other oddities to upper-class society were all invited.
Our favorite activity, besides wenching... no, even more than wenching, was to get terribly drunk and then go hunting. We were young and foolish, and we did love roasting boar on a spit.

But that night, our prey seemed smarter than normal, as difficult to tell as that is when drunk. The beast got the better of me and gored me horribly. It spilled my guts and I thought I would surely die.

True. I was weak and spent months in bed, contemplating my own mortality and becoming irrationally fearful of death. My father was greatly concerned with my inability to heal, so he called for a friend of his, a young but powerful wizard named Halaster.
That was a long time ago, and my lycanthropy adds to my skill in battle considerably. I was no slouch at hunting back then, either. The prey was just more intelligent this time.
I yield to you, in supplication most proper towards an enemy so skilled. I have given my all, to the very letter of the deal, and the mad fool of a wizard cannot deny that I did my best to slay you.

I was weak and spent months in bed, contemplating my own mortality and becoming irrationally fearful of death. My father was greatly concerned with my inability to heal, so he called for a friend of his, a powerful wizard named Halaster.

Halaster discovered that I was a lycanthrope, which pleased me. When I told him what I truly feared, he offered me hope, in the form of a potion of youth. I was warned that it was also a poison, but I didn't care, since he had an antidote. He gave me a small dose, and I was back to my old self.

That is an insightful way of looking at it. Yes, my friends and I returned to our wild lifestyle, and I made them drink the potion as part of our joining ritual. An eternal revelry. But the antidote was only temporary - and Halaster moved here, Undermountain.

Of course, I was still a lycanthrope, but my friends and I returned to our wild lifestyle, and I made them drink the potion as part of our joining ritual. An eternal revelry. But the antidote was only temporary - and Halaster moved here, Undermountain.

We followed, begging, asking, demanding that he tell us how to make the antidote. Instead he simply laughed and forced us to live here and fight for his amusement, in exchange for the potion. And that is my tale.

Halaster brews the potion somewhere else in this horrid dungeon, in another lieutenant's realm. I have not been able to determine where he keeps the recipe, but there is a certain smell in the air from the brewing process. I have a totem, an extension of myself, that you could take with you.

Halaster has made certain that I cannot leave this room without taking great damage, but if I had the recipe, I could brew the drink I need to keep me healthy. This would make it possible for me to leave... I hope. I must take that chance. We must not be caged!
Be straightforward with me, that I might know my fate.
Then perhaps Malar will! I will be caged no longer!
Excellent. Here is a totem I carved of myself. Just use it and you shall be able to converse with me. Malar help you in your hunt. Oh, one more thing before you leave.

Please, have mercy. I know that your blood must boil with the desire to kill me, for I would feel no different myself. Yet I ask that you listen to my tale and perhaps we can find some common ground, aye? Of course we can!
There is still a long way to go before you can face Halaster. Help me in this and I will help you reach him. I look forward to your battles against my peers, and more, my superiors.
I know that you have defeated the rest of my peers, but soon you will face the Inner Circle, his elite generals. I will help you in your battle against them. Help me and I will willingly help you.
There now, I have opened a portal that shall transport you back to the surface, where you can find another entrance into a different part of Undermountain. Best of luck!

Once I have the recipe, I will be free of Halaster's control, and I will give you part of my life force, my incredible speed, for the rest of your life. I offer you the one thing that has set me above the pack.
While I have rarely been curious about anything beyond pleasure, I  know that some value it above gold or wine. Ask your questions and I will do my best to answer.
The revelries will continue, though far from here. I will not have the life potion to give out, so no more will be poisoned. Pleasure and freedom are all that I seek. Why, what would you have me do?
Just curious about my plans? Very well. Now you know. We wish only to put great distance between Halaster and ourselves. We shall revel in our freedom!
Chaos can be pleasurable, though never a goal I sought in and of itself. If that is your demand for my freedom then I shall do as you ask. I shall reap chaos such as this world has never known.
That is very much my goal. We were never interested in destroying others, though some were hurt when they got in our way. I never found great pleasure in killing or hurting the innocent.
That is... not something I had ever considered. I suppose that my freedom could be worth a little do-gooding. Very well, I promise to try to help others. Perhaps I shall find pleasure in the deed.

Too true, too true. The drink was upon me. I know that your blood must boil with the desire to kill me, for I would feel no different myself. Yet I ask that you listen to my tale and perhaps we can find some common ground, aye? Of course we can!
Have you any other questions?

What I know about Halaster is very little. When I met him first, he was sympathetic, ready to help and generally very cheerful. When he brewed potions for me, his mood was always different. Sometimes he was brusque and cold. Other times he seemed angry.
Those who think that Halaster has only recently gone mad just haven't known him long enough. Certainly he seems to be worse lately, but he has been off-kilter for centuries. Other questions?

I pace these rooms like a trapped animal, and then I realize that it's not just a clever simile, but that my essence is that of a wild animal! I am not like a trapped animal, I *am* a trapped animal. No wonder my soul is so restless. Is there something you wanted?
May Malar grant you the skill of the hunter and the fury of the hunted.
What would you like, my head? An arm, perhaps? I offer you a powerful boon, which cannot be truly given until I am free of my old master.

Halaster has a recipe for a potion, an antidote, that keeps me alive. If I had that recipe, then I would be able to join you in battle and not be dependent on Halaster's moments of sanity when he remembers to brew the drink.

I pace these rooms like a trapped animal, and then I realize that it's not just a clever simile, but that my essence is that of a wild animal! I am not like a trapped animal, I *am* a trapped animal. But now you have the recipe and the wild hunt may begin again!
What could you possibly want it for? This is not the elixir that grants eternal, if flawed, life. It is only an antidote for a poison you have never sipped.

You have the word of Lord Antoine Baccha, Vizier de Guise! That is sacrosanct and binding. Any who know of me know that when I give my word, I hold to it! I will assist you, just give me the cure, please!

You certainly have. I know that your blood must boil with the desire to kill me, for I would feel no different myself. Yet I ask that you listen to my tale and perhaps we can find some common ground, aye? Of course we can!
I will not remain a prisoner here! My soul cries out for freedom, even if it means my death!
Use the totem and you shall have the speed of a rushing boar, for all your life. It is all the power I can grant you; I hope that it is sufficient. Now, we are free! Malar aid you in your hunt.
I was told that one of his clones has expired, but that does nothing for me, except give me some small measure of pleasure. Without the recipe, I am still trapped here. Please, give me the recipe.
Then I shall fight you to death, if I must! On guard, peasant!

The name is Lord Antoine Baccha, Vizier de Guise, and I wish it was a great pleasure to meet you, but I have only been defeated so soundly once before. The first time I was a dead-drunk mortal and was attacked by a lycanthrope.

Halaster brews the potion I need somewhere else in this horrid dungeon. I have not been able to determine where he keeps the recipe, but there is a certain smell in the air from the brewing process. I have an artifact, an extension of myself, that you could take with you.

I and my friends were drunk and went hunting. I was attacked by a were-boar and infected with lycanthropy. While bedridden and grievously ill, I began to fear my mortality. My father became worried about my apparent lack of rehabilitation and called on a powerful friend.
I have a sudden inclination to disembowel you.
Your feeble efforts were no match for my power!
Tell me what happened.
You mean those whose lack of social graces could be laughed at?
Sounds like fun.
Go on.
You were a challenge, but I have bested you fairly.
Well, alcohol does tend to lower one's reflexes.
Gutted by a swine and you thought you could challenge me?
Yet you survived.
But you were still a were-creature.
So you look at this lycanthropy as an extension of your old self, do you?
Better than your old self, I would say. More powerful than ever.
I think I'd rather kill you.
Really?
I've heard enough. Time for me to kill you.
And what do you want from me?
So now you work for him?
I have made a decision.
I think I am just going to kill you.
I can't help you.
I will help you find the recipe.
What kind of reward can you offer?
I have some questions for you.
What would you do if I helped you leave here?
Do as you think best. I care little.
I suppose I could listen.
Go forth and bring chaos to the world!
Just be free and try not to hurt others.
Protect the innocent and use your powers for good.
Can you tell me what Halaster used to be like?
I should be going.
Who are you?
I have decided to kill you, instead.
Could I get part of my reward now?
Could you remind me what I am looking for?
I'm thinking of keeping it.
I don't know that I can trust you.
You can't have it.
I figure if I have it, I control you.
I just don't want you to have it.
As for my reward?
I think I am just going to kill you.
Here is the recipe.

Are you having fun in the dungeon? Want to do some trading?
No problem. What would you like to ask?

Happily, the dark demon is still in his lair. Harat is one of the only ones who stays here willingly. You have no idea how difficult it is to get powerful creatures to live in a dungeon! (I used to rhyme, some of the time, but now it's a crime, so I can't.)
Always happy to oblige.
I can try to answer your questions, but I don't promise to know the right answers. I don't really know very much about how things work.
Very well. Did you want to go into Undermountain again, or did you want to do some trading first?

There are lots of creatures in Undermountain, many of which are very powerful. I don't know if anyone other than Halaster knows how many there are. And since Halaster seems quite mad, I don't know that even he could tell you.
Shhh! I don't think you should say his name. That's the evil I was telling you about. I know they say that he was once not so bad, but now he has completely lost his mind.
You have to! He has become a terror and rules the creatures of Undermountain with a crushing grip of despair.

I know that he has become such a terrible tyrant that all of the creatures of Undermountain fear to cross him, or even to speak to him. They say that he goes into a frothing frenzy whenever an adventurer dares to succeed, that he kills more than the adventurers do.
Some think he has always been mad, but others claim that the madness was feigned, but for so long that now it seems to have completely taken over his mind.

They also say that this Halaster person likes to drink tea. But the thing is, he never used to like tea. Sort of a strange thing to develop a taste for after hundreds of years. Really! Tea! It doesn't get any madder than that!
Have you? Oh, well, maybe it's not so bad then. I was just worried. That Halaster has really lost his grasp of reality, from what I was told. And he certainly destroyed my friends without any qualms.

Sadly, the dark demon has fled. And here I was trying to make Harat a god. How disappointing. He was one of the only ones who stayed here willingly. You have no idea how difficult it is to get powerful creatures to live in a dungeon! (I used to rhyme, some of the time, but now it's a crime, so I can't.)

You won't stop, just because it's Halaster, will you? That would be awful. He's gotten so mean and cruel. It is time someone stood up to him. Since the Lords of Waterdeep have known about him for years and done nothing to stop him, who else will, if you won't?
I really hope you will. It is so important that someone defeats him. He can't get away with his evil, treacherous ways.
Thank you, thank you, thank you! Oh, I knew I could count on you the moment you stepped in here. I knew you were a real brave one!

I think I might have seen something like that, only it was a little finger, so it was only a rod, not a staff. Come to think of it, it might not have been so much a giant's finger as a dragon's claw. Sorry, I guess that's not much help.
I know lots of widows. I know Widow Lockney, who is an old, poor widow who sells wrinkly apples for a living. I know Widow Latisi, who has been married three times and is still young and beautiful.
If you stand in just the right place outside her window at night... but you aren't likely interested in that. There are more widows, but I'm not sure about a Hagatha.

Hee, hee, she is the talk of all the boy orphans. We treat her nice and bring her little gifts sometimes. But you wouldn't want to marry her, no. Her husbands all end up dead in some horrible fashion. Her first accidentally fell into a well, with the cover still on it.

Her second husband hung himself, and then stabbed himself fifteen times, twice in the back. It's amazing the stories that guards will believe if you pay them properly. The last husband died in his sleep.

Widow Latisi claimed that he was a follower of Ilmater and his arms got very flexible from whipping his own back. That's all I overheard. The guards chased us away before they continued the investigation. That was before her third husband died in his sleep.

Well, when you sleep with a pillow over your face, these things are bound to happen. The widow claimed that he felt bad about snoring and was trying not to disturb her. That's about all I know about Widow Latisi.

Sadly, the dark demon is dead. And Harat thought he was a god. How disappointing. He was one of the only ones who stayed here willingly. You have no idea how difficult it is to get powerful creatures to live in a dungeon! (I used to rhyme, some of the time, but now it's a crime, so I can't.)
I see, now! She seemed so sad, or at least she sounded sad, when I heard about her. I felt sorry for her. But then, there are a lot of sad stories that come out of Undermountain.
I don't know if she killed any of my friends, but she must have killed lots of people and monsters to become as powerful as they say she is.

A recipe? No, my parents never taught me to cook, so I don't really bother with that sort of thing. And with them being dead, I don't know who will teach me to cook. Now you've made me sad. Can we talk about something else, please?
The wereboar guy? He seems to have a really strange idea of fun and friends, I think. But then, my friends were a little strange too, I suppose. They didn't change shape, or anything.

I don't really know very much about him, except that if he really wanted to leave, what's stopping him? If I had his powers, I would take matters into my own hands. And dragging his friends into it? Seems selfish, but what would I know about it?

Oh, wait, let me look. Here! This is it... oh, no, wait, I was wrong. I thought maybe I had one, but it turns out it's just a necklace with a fly on it, not a beetle. That's what a scarab is. I learned that from Big Timmy, who liked bugs.
Of course, Big Timmy is dead now. There is a hurting in my chest when I think about that. I'm sorry. I wish I could have helped you.
Is that what the insect-thing was called? I don't really know much about her, except that those creatures that follow her make tunnels and I wonder if maybe they help build Undermountain.

If they do, then what happens if they are gone? Does Undermountain stop changing, or will it continue no matter what? These are the things that can keep me awake at night. How much control does the evil have in Undermountain?

Should the sun be allowed to go away, if it tires of trekking across the sky, even though we would all probably die without its light? I don't know. Where do we draw the line? I'm just a kid; why are you asking me these things?

I still have the amulet to control the hivemother, Maggris. I am pleased that she neither escaped nor died. It shall make replacing her much easier. (Bugs. I hates bugs. Except with a sweet elven wine.)

The sun isn't intelligent? I thought it was a god. Lathandar or something like that. I guess even gods have limits on their freedom. That's what I was told, but I don't really know that much. I'm sure you've noticed, I'm just a kid.

So how are you enjoying the dungeon? It sure is a fun place, isn't it? I really like it, or I would if I could go in there, which I can't because I am far too young. My dad said I'm precocious, but I don't know what that means.
Have fun down there.
Of course you can. I always enjoy trading.
Feel free to lay down here and rest, then. It's a nice warehouse, isn't it? So roomy, drafty, and yet homey.
You aren't doing anything very exciting. You might want to go down into my secret adventuring place now.

Boring! What are you, some kind of pacifist? Or are you scared? Isn't that a great word? I just learned it. A guard was beating on a merchant and called him a dirty pacifist. I guess that meant something about his refusing to join the guards. I think he was just scared. Is that your problem?
I don't blame you if you are scared. I am scared, but then, I'm only a kid. What's your excuse? Well, do what you want.
Really? That's something I can do. I just thought you were done.
Then what are you waiting for? I don't have time to wait around here all day... well, I guess I do, but that's not the point.

Maggris took her daughters and fled Undermountain. I suppose it was time for her to leave, though this really slows things down with my work in Undermountain. (I'm going to need a shovel and a pick. Oh, and a really big tribe of goblins.)
Oh, this is so exciting! I wish I could go with you, but you will make certain you come back and tell me how things are going, right? Hopefully you will keep safe.

The thing that killed my friends is hiding somewhere down there. Please kill it so that no one else has to suffer like my friends. Here, just to help you, see if there is anything you would like to buy.
Shhh! The dungeon's still moving! Talk to me in a second, please.
Who are you? Are you a brave and powerful adventurer? I sure hope you are. There are lots of brave people in Waterdeep, but most of them don't come in here. I'm sure glad you did.
My name is Timmy, but most people call me Little Timmy, because of my friend Big Timmy. But he died, so I guess I could just be Timmy, except I'm used to being Little Timmy now. What's your name?

A mystery! I thought you might be someone powerful. I really need your help. My friends and I always play in the back streets of Waterdeep and sometimes we would sneak into a warehouse like this, just to see if there was anything to do. That's what we were doing here, when we heard a rumbling and saw that door appear.

Oh, thank you! I was so scared before you came. My friends and I always play in the back streets of Waterdeep and sometimes we would sneak into a warehouse like this, just to see if there was anything to do. That's what we were doing here, when we heard a rumbling and saw that door appear.

My friends and I always play in the back alleys and sometimes we would sneak into a warehouse like this, just to see if there was anything to do. That's what we were doing here, when we heard a rumbling and saw that door appear.
At first we were afraid to enter, but then Big Timmy said we were too afraid to go in and we wanted to prove we were not afraid so we went in and Big Timmy came too.

Yes, that is exactly it! We didn't want to be thought chickens, so we went in. But then there were monsters and bad things and a horrid, powerful evil that came and took my friends and now they're all gone or dead or something.

Maggris is dead, as you know, since it was you who reduced her to splatterings of ichor and chitin. Not that I mind terribly, since that was your job, but that really slows things down with my work in Undermountain. (I'm going to need a shovel and a pick. Oh, and a really big tribe of goblins.)

I didn't want the others to think I was chicken, and I think they thought the same, so we went in. But then there were monsters and bad things and a horrid, powerful evil that came and took my friends and now they're all gone or dead or something.

I... I guess it was, but we didn't want people to think we were chicken, so we went in. But then there were monsters and bad things and a horrid, powerful evil that came and took my friends and now they're all gone or dead or something.

I ran away and escaped and tried to get grown ups to come and find my friends and kill the bad things, but they all keep dying. Even big, tough warriors and other adventurers have died, so I am trying to find the bravest, best adventurer of all.
Well... you see, they don't exactly listen to us street orphans. They usually try to chase us and put us in those terrible orphanages, so no. But what do they have that an adventurer doesn't have?

But I haven't told you what I've learned about where the door leads. One of the adventurers came back to trade with me, and he said that this place is actually a door to Undermountain. Now adventurers pay me so they can go in.
But it turns out this is a special adventuring place called Undermountain, and you might like it, unless you're chicken? I sure hope not, because I thought you looked brave when you came in here.
One of the adventurers came back to trade with me, and he said that this place is actually a door to Undermountain. So I have been getting people to pay me so they can enter.

There was this one guy who came in here and he was a little chicken, I think, and he tried to rob me, but I didn't have any gold or silver or copper, or any other colored dragons, so I let him see my secret adventure place and he gouged his own eyes out. You won't do that, will you?
So what do you think? Will you go into the special adventuring place? Can you destroy the evil thing that killed all my friends? Are you brave enough?

Oh, good. That sounds really great, except that you haven't told me what the decision is, but other than that, it sounds swell. Maybe before you go in, you could buy one of the treasures that I found. So?

Hagatha, the widowed giantess, waits and mourns her long dead husband. Soon she will have to join him, I fear. (And then I will have some cloud giant bones to work with. I think it is time I made a magical chair. With nice soft cushions.)
There is always a reward, but I just have some poor treasures that adventurers were willing to trade me; nothing like the exciting things you might find down there. The reward is in the dungeon.

Really? But what about my friends? Well, if you change your mind, I will do a few things for you. First, if you go in, when you come back I will allow you to buy and sell me things. I give much better rates than the monsters down there do.
Secondly, um... nope, I was wrong, there was only the one thing.
I will gladly show you what I have to sell, if you will simply agree to go into the special adventuring place and destroy the evil hiding in the depths. So, how about it? Feeling adventuresome?

This is so exciting! I wish I could go with you, but you will make certain you come back and tell me how things are going, right? Oh, and here is a special map and a journal, to help you on your way. Hopefully they will help you keep safe.

The thing that killed my friends is hiding somewhere down there. Please kill it so that no one else has to suffer like my friends. Here, just to help you, see if there is anything you would like to buy.

That's a good idea. I once scratched at my arm until it bled and then I got sick and that's when my mom told me that my puppy had died. So if you don't want puppies to die, you shouldn't hurt yourself. That's the moral of the story.
All good stories have morals, but sometimes they are hidden really deep and you have to adventure through many dungeons to find the morals. So would you like to see my special adventuring place?

There are many names for it and I know that some people call it Undermountain, but I think it should have a better name like the Whimsy Fun Place, or the Infinite Dungeons. But my friends all died there, so maybe a bleak name like Undermountain is good too.

We found this secret entrance and I would only charge you one gold piece to get in, which is a real bargain. Unless you don't want to pay me, then you can go in for free, but it would be nice if you bought some of my treasures then.

Hagatha, the widowed giantess, has gone to put her long dead husband to rest. Then she will probably join him. (So much for my cloud giant bones. I was really longing to make that magical chair. With nice soft cushions.)

You've never heard of Undermountain? Why, it has entrances all over the world, but this is a newer one that we just... found. Or maybe it found us, who is to say? But there are stories about this place, like once I heard that a man entered, died, and got his ghost stuck in a mirror.

And then there was this lady and this tiger and her father and a man who loved her, but he chose a door, but then nothing really worked right so the guy who was the boss in there, he sent them all away. It... changes. Once you experience some of it, I might be able to explain it better.

Sometimes people bring me stuff to buy, or they get hurt and I get some of their stuff when I help them out. I have new things all the time. Did you want to buy something, or are you going to go in now?

Well, since you are willing to trade with me, I don't need to charge you the one gold piece. I make more off of trading than I ever will for charging you a gold at a time. I hope you like the things I have collected.

I am trying to save enough gold to build a marker to remember my friends. I think you are very brave for going in and I want to encourage you. Maybe I will just let you go for free. Just bring interesting things back to trade with me. That would be nice.
I think he was ripped apart by a pack of ghouls. It was very messy. I think he might be a zombie now.
Sometimes people come back and tell me, but sometimes I just... make it up. My dad says that I have a very active imagination.

I'm not making any of it up. Honest. My friends died and then my dad, well, not my real father, just the orphans' protector. We make sure we bring him food and... gifts, and he keeps the adults and guards away from us, as much as possible. Or he used to.
I am. He's not my real father, just the orphans' protector. We make sure we bring him food and... gifts, and he keeps the adults and guards away from us, as much as possible. But he's dead now.

He was the first person I told and he went in, but he hardly got in the door when he was attacked and eaten by harpies. I don't like harpies much. They're pretty ugly. But there are lots of monsters in Undermountain. Lots of ways to die.

Hagatha, the widowed giantess is dead, just like her husband. Probably for the best. She was always so sad. (And now I have some cloud giant bones to work with. I think it is time I made a magical chair. With nice soft cushions.)
No.
Yes. Although there was this one time when I had a cough and it wouldn't go away, but then it finally did and that was when the screaming stopped.
What screaming?
Oh, but you can't go yet! They killed all my friends and someone has to kill the evil thing that's in Undermountain! Otherwise we are all doomed!
If you change your mind, you can come back. I have also collected some treasure I could sell you. You might want to look at it, if you are interested in that kind of thing.

Well... maybe not everybody, but plenty of good people, and a few bad ones, will die and it will be your fault, because you were too chicken to go in and stop them. And I think that I might be doomed because I saw them. I am afraid they will try to kill me.

Of course! Would you like to go into the special adventuring place now? The first part isn't too bad, but you have to watch out for the... um... there's something there that you should watch out for... I can't remember.
Well, I'm glad if it stopped because I've never really liked screaming and once my mother said that I shouldn't scream because it wouldn't hurt, but then it did, so I screamed.
Oh, no. Once I was pretending to be a rat, but the other rats didn't buy it, so they wouldn't play with me and just kept running away. So I killed them, because that's what you do with rats.

Is that what you would like to be in it? Because some people don't like rats and some people say that everyone should have to kill a few rats when they start, but I always thought people should have a choice. Why do you like rats so much, anyway?

Because you keep talking about them. You should go into my special adventuring place, because there are lots of magic things and stuff and bits.

Food! It comes with the smells of the fleshy-ones. It comes with malice in its heart. End it, rend it, feed it to us, spawn of my blood.
Torn! Gone! So many lives in such short time. Such power to behold. Halt your attacks, food, that we may speak.

That is the name of the He, yes. The He who holds us, and when we die, the He who takes our hivedaughter and begins again, with no freedom for her. The Maggris, hivemother, is old now. We will be dead and then the eggs shall not be smashed, but one shall grow and become the Maggris.

It was that way with us, when the Maggris before us grew old. Then the He allowed us to live, fed the Maggris of old to us, that we become the hivemother anew. It is not like eating you, food. To eat a hivemother brings us memories. We remember all, eternal. We remember how it starts.

The He came to our nests with food that fought us, those you call orcs and goblins. They came in numbers greater than our males. They killed the males, took our eggs, and the He demanded service of the Maggris.

The He came to us in the place you food call Mulhorand. The He came and took us and brought us here, working and digging. We objected. We wanted freedom. The He went back and found the holy scarab. It crushes our mind. It consumes our will. We have no freedom.
The food of Mulhorand called the holy scarab by the name: the Scarab Amulet of Imaskar. It has power to speak in the hivemind, too powerful for the Magris to overcome.

Go. We know not where the He has hidden the amulet. Find for us this scarab, and when it is ours, great power will we give you. Here is the egg of our hivedaughter. Take and use her. She is linked to me and we shall help you find the scarab.
The mind of the food is foreign to us. That is why we speak in the halting words of the food, not with the grace of the hivetongue. We cannot see your decision, so tell us.
Then you side with the He. Since the He is not here, your power is without his power. Therefore, we take our chances to face you now, and face the He later.
We will be with you, through our daughter. If the end comes and the He you should face, we will help you. If we have the scarab. Without, we have no control. No power to face the He.

We are but one of the soldiers that the He uses to guard himself. Others will try to take you, but with our power, you can face these. You will need strong. Here is way out. Find new dungeon. Be swift.

Fear. We have fear that you come to drive us to our deaths. Logic. This must prevail for both sides to seek... your word is satisfaction? Yes. You are powerful. The He, whom the food calls Halaster, is powerful. You could be the power to free us, or the power to kill us... maybe both.

Defeated are our peers, the soldiers of the He. Yet, the He has others, more powerful, waiting, biding time, that will try to destroy you. Our power will make you strong. You will need strong, facing the Inner Circle. Here is way out. Find new dungeon. Be swift.

The cold is not for the best, when we remember the warmth of our home. But most of all, it is the lack of freedom. We move, we build, we destroy, we rebuild, we tunnel, we dig, we tire. The He commands too much.
Always, but more of late than before. Everything changes too fast, too soon, so that more and more males are produced, but die quickly. It tires us. That is why we offer so much power to you.
The words of your tongue... confound us at times. We try, if you are patient. What knowledge do you seek?
We move, we build, we destroy, we rebuild, we tunnel, we dig, we tire. The cold is not for the best, when we remember the warmth of our home. But mostly, we hate the lack of freedom.

Hate is consuming and we spend much time hating the He. Everything changes too fast, too soon, so that more and more males are produced, but die quickly. It tires us. That is why we offer so much power to you.
We know little of the food who live there, for we had food that did not fight back. Here we came and had to eat what was here, for our food that burrowed in the ground was much harder to find.

Home was warmer, with much of the red heat in the earth, that we could use to warm the tunnels and the nests. The tunnels swarmed with life, the males worked with diligence, the hivedaughters served with love and the food never talked back.
That is all we care to tell. There are infinitely more memories, but they are not for food. Not even powerful, friend food.
They are what we dream of. What the Maggris must lead her people towards. But, they are sad too. They make the desire for freedom burn more.

Always good to have more power! We are the Maggris. We are eternal knowledge. We are self-destruction. We are the mind of all, the great guide, the constant buzz, the hivemother, and once we were free!
Time. Enough about our home. Is your mind full yet, or have you other questions?
It is hard to answer, but we answer what we can.
Is your mind full, or have you more questions?
Males? They are not hivesons, they are just males. They work and do as they are told, but they have no more mind than the leaf on a tree that turns and follows the sun across the sky.
When a hivedaughter dies, there is pain. Not so with males. They are of no consequence, except for the effort of their birth. They have no wants but to serve the Maggris. That is all.

The Maggris was hivemother, but the hivedaughters lived and served until it was time. Then the Maggris would give herself to her favorite. The hivedaughter would devour the Maggris and become one with her.
Death. The memories live on, but there is no consciousness. No discussion between hivemother and hivedaughter once the body dies. We are mortal too, but our deeds are remembered.

We do know about sarcasm, but we can not be certain if you use it or if you are sincere. It is a lovely relationship. A loving relationship. A relationship of long tradition and history, where there is better understanding than food could ever know.
Before, it was a gift from hivemother to hivedaughter. Now it is forced, and the He chooses the one to be bestowed. That hivedaughter might not be the strong choice for the Maggris.

There is nothing you need do. So long as she is in the egg, our hivedaughter will have no need for food, water, or warmth. To avoid: cold of any greatness can possibly kill, as can a direct blow to the egg.
We are the Maggris. We are eternal knowledge. We are self-destruction. We are the mind of all, the great guide, the constant buzz, the hivemother, and once we were free!

Without freedom, her life belongs to the He. That is no life, for the He will certainly smash her, as the He has done for such long time. With you, the hivedaughter has a chance for freedom. The whole hive has a chance for freedom.

While our hivedaughter is in her egg, she is better protected than you might assume. A direct blow to the egg might kill her, but otherwise she should be safe. We are pleased that you show concern for the hivedaughter.
